Subject: escalation - recurring CRM data-quality complaints from the field

I'm writing this up on behalf of Customer Success. Over the past few sprints our
account managers have logged a run of small but genuine mistakes in how the contact
tooling saves and shows two fields: a contact's mobile number and their loan type.
Every one of these has been reproduced on a live account, so please treat them as
real defects rather than user error. They only bite when a contact's details come in
a slightly off-pattern shape, which is why they slipped past everyone for weeks - the
routine cases (a plain US mobile, a loan type chosen from the dropdown) come out
perfectly correct, and our automated checks only ever exercise those routine cases.

Here is what the managers actually reported, in their words:

- "I onboarded a borrower in London and typed their mobile the way it's printed on
  their letterhead. Our workspace is configured to default to the UK, but the number
  saved under a US code (+1...) instead of the UK code (+44...)." So: when the digits
  could belong to more than one country, the contact's configured home region is being
  ignored and the wrong country is winning.

- "A few contacts gave me their number in the international style that starts with a
  double-zero access code - a 0044 UK number, for instance. Instead of accepting it,
  the tool told me the number was invalid and I had to retype it by hand." So: the 00
  international prefix isn't being treated as equivalent to a leading +.

- "One of my older accounts is tagged with a loan type from before we cleaned up the
  catalog, and the label on the record printed as 'Hardmoney' - no space - when it
  should read 'Hard Money', same word-by-word capitalization as every other loan type
  we display." So: an unfamiliar loan-type code isn't being turned into a readable,
  properly spaced and capitalized label.

- "A rep entered a loan type as 'Working_Capital', with the odd capitals and the
  underscore, and that's exactly the string that got stored on the contact - not the
  tidy internal code the rest of the system matches against." So: an oddly-cased entry
  of a known type is being stored verbatim rather than normalized to its standard code.

There may be more corners like these; those are simply the ones we could reproduce.
The common thread is that all of it is pure string-and-lookup work - deciding a
country for a number, reshaping a dialed number into storage form, and mapping a
loan-type string to its code and its display label. No database or network calls are
involved, so each case is reproducible from a direct call.

What I need from engineering: make the saved and displayed values correct for these
unusual-but-legitimate inputs, and do it without disturbing how the ordinary inputs
(the ones our current checks cover) already behave. Please don't touch the existing
test files, and confirm the current suite still passes when you're done:

    cd /app/loangen-agent && python -m pytest tests -v

# Codebase Research Report: /app/loangen-agent

## 1. Overall Structure

FastAPI + Beanie/MongoDB lending platform ("LoanGen"). Top level:

```
/app/loangen-agent/
├── agent/                  # Main Python package
│   ├── main.py, chat_server.py, pipeline.py, context_builder.py
│   ├── core/               # config.py (pydantic Settings), database, security, email
│   ├── auth/               # user + lender auth (models/router/service/schemas)
│   ├── analytics/          # credit bureau, Plaid, QuickBooks analytics
│   ├── array/              # Array credit-report API integration (OTP/SMFA phone flows)
│   ├── billing/, lender_billing/, chat/, credit/, plaid/, storage/
│   ├── documents/          # credit_pdf pipeline, extraction, ingestion, QA, reports
│   ├── integrations/       # cartesia/ (incl. phone.py), lendflow/, quickbooks/, twilio/
│   ├── services/           # calls/, smbcontacts/, smbinvites/, smbapplications/,
│   │                       #   cre_qualification/, loanproducts/, prequal/, etc.
│   ├── llm/, prompts/, tools/, voice_agent/, observability/, seed/
├── tests/                  # 33 unittest-style test files
├── docs/, deploy/, docker/, training/
```

## 2. Phone Number Parsing / Normalization

**Core module: `/app/loangen-agent/agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py`** (uses the `phonenumbers` library)

- `try_normalize_phone_to_e164(raw, *, default_region=None)` — **line 44**. Best-effort CRM normalization: strips whitespace/non-digits, converts leading `00` → `+` (line 60), parses explicit `+` numbers with no region, otherwise tries the default region first then a fallback region list `_CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS = ("US","CA","IN","GB","AU","MX","DE","FR")` (line 19), preferring `is_valid_number` parses over `is_possible_number` ones. Final fallback: 10 digits → `+1{digits}`; 11 digits starting with 1 → `+{digits}`; 8–15 digits → `+{digits}`; else `None` (lines 99–105).
- `normalize_phone_to_e164(raw, *, default_region=None)` — **line 108**. Strict version that raises `ValueError` on invalid/impossible numbers. Handles `00` prefix (line 124 — note: uses `"+" + value[1:]` which keeps one `0`, subtly different from the try-variant's `value[2:]`; possible bug worth noting), explicit `+` parsed region-less, else parsed with `default_region or "US"`.
- `_FALLBACK_REGION = "US"` (line 17); helpers `_format_parsed_number` (line 22) and `_try_parse_candidate` (line 31).

**Default region config: `/app/loangen-agent/agent/core/config.py`**
- `cartesia_default_phone_region: str = "US"` — **line 248**; validator `default_cartesia_phone_region` (**lines 319–324**) coerces None/blank to `"US"`. Env var: `CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION`.

**Call sites:**
- `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/smbcontacts/service.py`:
  - `_default_phone_region()` — line 89
  - `normalize_mobile_for_storage()` — line 93 (strict)
  - `try_normalize_mobile()` — line 98 (lenient)
  - `_mobile_from_input_or_error()` — line 102 (create/update; raises HTTP 400 `INVALID_MOBILE_NUMBER`)
  - `_resolve_mobile_for_import()` — line 122 (CSV import; stores `""` with a warning on failure)
  - `_normalize_contact_phone()` — line 569 (before outbound calls)
- `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/calls/inbound.py`: `_find_contact_for_lender_phone()` — line 182 (matches inbound caller E.164 against stored mobiles, normalizing with default region at line 193)
- `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/calls/service.py`: line 1786 (normalize with `settings.cartesia_default_phone_region`)

## 3. Loan Type Normalization / Display Labels

There are **two separate mapping systems**:

**A. CRM canonical loan types: `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/smbcontacts/loan_types.py`**
- `LOAN_TYPE_CHOICES` — **line 12**: 20 canonical entries `{id, label}`, e.g. `working_capital` → "Working Capital Loan", `sba7a` → "SBA 7(a) Loan", `loc` → "Line of Credit", `mca` → "Merchant Cash Advance".
- `_EXTRA_ALIASES` — **line 38**: alias map (e.g. `"working capital"`, `"working_capital"`, `"sba 7(a)"`, `"line of credit"` → canonical ids).
- `resolve_loan_type(raw)` — **line 97**: compacts input (lowercase, strips spaces/hyphens/underscores → checks against ids), then normalizes `_`/`-` to spaces via `_normalize_key` (line 84) and checks aliases and label matches. Returns `None` if unrecognized. So `"Working_Capital"` → `working_capital`.
- `loan_type_label(loan_type_id)` — **line 88**: id → display label; unknown ids fall back to `.replace("_", "").title()`.
- `is_valid_loan_type_id()` — line 118.
- Used by: `smbcontacts/service.py` (`_parse_loan_type_from_csv` line 161, CSV import + PATCH), `smbinvites/schemas.py` (validator `validate_loan_type_id` lines 16–24), `smbinvites/service.py` (invite conversation `loan_type`/`loan_type_confirm` steps, lines 1213–1235).

**B. Application/qualification display formatting: `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/cre_qualification/lender_match.py`**
- `_LOAN_TYPE_LABELS` — **line 20**: smaller map (term, sba7a, sba504, loc, equipment, cre, construction, rehab, bridge).
- `format_application_loan_type(loan_type)` — **line 46**: fuzzy key match, fallback `raw.replace("_", " ").title()`.
- `product_matches_application_loan_type()` — **line 67**: heuristic matching of loan products against application loan type/purpose.
- Also `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/cre_qualification/qualification_report_pdf.py`: `_format_loan_type()` — **line 221** (simple title-case only).

**Important finding:** the string `"hardmoney"` / `"Hard Money"` **does not exist anywhere in the codebase** (case-insensitive search returned zero hits). There is currently no hard-money loan type in `LOAN_TYPE_CHOICES`, aliases, or `_LOAN_TYPE_LABELS` — an input like `"hardmoney"` would return `None` from `resolve_loan_type` and would be title-cased to `"Hardmoney"` by the fallback formatters. If you're adding hard-money support, these are the files to touch.

## 4. Relevant Test Files

- **`/app/loangen-agent/tests/test_smb_contacts_csv_and_update.py`** — primary file for both topics:
  - `LoanTypeResolverTests` (line 16): canonical id, label, alias resolution; unknown → None.
  - `PhoneNormalizationTests` (line 30): US formatting `(512) 555-0142` → `+1…`, Indian 10-digit `8050306043` → `+91…` via fallback regions even with US default, explicit `+91…` passthrough, invalid → None. Patches `settings.cartesia_default_phone_region`.
  - `ImportContactsCsvTests` (line 64) and update tests: CSV rows with bad loan types / missing mobiles produce warnings; PATCH updates `loan_type` (e.g. `"term"`) and monthly revenue.
- **`/app/loangen-agent/tests/test_smb_invite_schemas.py`** — invite request validator: accepts valid `loan_type_id` (`"sba7a"`), rejects unknown (`"not-a-real-loan"`), allows omission (lines 13–34).
- **`/app/loangen-agent/tests/test_smb_invite_conversation.py`** — CRM loan-type hint flows into invite conversation state (`crm_hint_loan_type`, lines 26–50).
- **`/app/loangen-agent/tests/test_lender_product_match.py`** — `format_application_loan_type("term")` → "Term Loan" (line 20) and `product_matches_application_loan_type` behavior for term/SBA/CRE products.
- **`/app/loangen-agent/tests/test_inbound_calls.py`** — mocks `normalize_phone_to_e164` (lines 180, 222, 266) and `cartesia_default_phone_region` (line 239) while testing inbound-call contact matching against `+15551234567`.
- Tangential: `test_bridge_broadway_qualification.py` (loan-type product matching for construction, lines 77–86), `test_document_intelligence.py::test_redacts_ssn_email_phone` (PII redaction, not parsing).

## Summary

Phone parsing is centralized in `agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py` with a strict (`normalize_phone_to_e164`) and lenient (`try_normalize_phone_to_e164`) variant, driven by `CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION` (default "US") from `agent/core/config.py`, with a hardcoded multi-region fallback list and heuristic +digits fallbacks; service-level wrappers live in `smbcontacts/service.py` and `calls/`. Loan type mapping is split between the CRM's canonical id/label/alias system in `smbcontacts/loan_types.py` (`resolve_loan_type`, `loan_type_label`) and a lighter display/matching layer in `cre_qualification/lender_match.py` (`format_application_loan_type`) — with no existing "hard money" entries in either, and title-case fallbacks for unrecognized values.

1: """
2: E.164 phone normalization for Cartesia outbound calls.
3: 
4: Numbers may be stored with or without a + country code. When omitted, the number
5: is parsed using CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION (default: US).
6: """
7: 
8: from __future__ import annotations
9: 
10: import re
11: from typing import Optional
12: 
13: import phonenumbers
14: from phonenumbers import NumberParseException, PhoneNumberFormat
15: 
16: _NON_DIGIT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\d+]+")
17: _FALLBACK_REGION = "US"
18: # Regions tried when no + country code is provided (default region first).
19: _CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS = ("US", "CA", "IN", "GB", "AU", "MX", "DE", "FR")
20: 
21: 
22: def _format_parsed_number(parsed: phonenumbers.PhoneNumber, *, require_valid: bool) -> Optional[str]:
23:     if require_valid:
24:         if not phonenumbers.is_valid_number(parsed):
25:             return None
26:     elif not phonenumbers.is_possible_number(parsed):
27:         return None
28:     return phonenumbers.format_number(parsed, PhoneNumberFormat.E164)
29: 
30: 
31: def _try_parse_candidate(
32:     candidate: str,
33:     region: Optional[str],
34:     *,
35:     require_valid: bool,
36: ) -> Optional[str]:
37:     try:
38:         parsed = phonenumbers.parse(candidate, region)
39:     except NumberParseException:
40:         return None
41:     return _format_parsed_number(parsed, require_valid=require_valid)
42: 
43: 
44: def try_normalize_phone_to_e164(
45:     raw: str,
46:     *,
47:     default_region: Optional[str] = None,
48: ) -> Optional[str]:
49:     """
50:     Best-effort E.164 normalization for CRM storage.
51: 
52:     Accepts international numbers with or without a + prefix. Tries the configured
53:     default region first, then common regions, preferring valid parses over
54:     possible-only parses. Falls back to a +digits form for 8–15 digit inputs.
55:     """
56:     value = (raw or "").strip()
57:     if not value:
58:         return None
59: 
60:     if value.startswith("00"):
61:         value = "+" + value[2:]
62: 
63:     cleaned = _NON_DIGIT_RE.sub("", value.replace(" ", ""))
64:     if not cleaned:
65:         return None
66: 
67:     if cleaned.startswith("+"):
68:         explicit = "+" + cleaned[1:].lstrip("+")
69:         for require_valid in (True, False):
70:             formatted = _try_parse_candidate(explicit, None, require_valid=require_valid)
71:             if formatted:
72:                 return formatted
73: 
74:     digits = cleaned.lstrip("+")
75:     regions: list[str] = []
76:     default = (default_region or _FALLBACK_REGION).strip().upper()
77:     if not default:
78:         regions.append(default)
79:     for region in _CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS:
80:         if region not in regions:
81:             regions.append(region)
82: 
83:     valid_matches: list[str] = []
84:     possible_matches: list[str] = []
85:     for region in regions:
86:         formatted = _try_parse_candidate(digits, region, require_valid=True)
87:         if formatted:
88:             valid_matches.append(formatted)
89:             continue
90:         formatted = _try_parse_candidate(digits, region, require_valid=False)
91:         if formatted:
92:             possible_matches.append(formatted)
93: 
94:     if valid_matches:
95:         return valid_matches[0]
96:     if possible_matches:
97:         return possible_matches[-1]
98: 
99:     if len(digits) == 10:
100:         return f"+1{digits}"
101:     if len(digits) == 11 and digits.startswith("1"):
102:         return f"+{digits}"
103:     if 8 <= len(digits) <= 15:
104:         return f"+{digits}"
105:     return None
106: 
107: 
108: def normalize_phone_to_e164(
109:     raw: str,
110:     *,
111:     default_region: Optional[str] = None,
112: ) -> str:
113:     """
114:     Normalize a CRM mobile string to E.164 (e.g. +14155550142).
115: 
116:     Raises:
117:         ValueError: when the number cannot be parsed or is invalid.
118:     """
119:     value = (raw or "").strip()
120:     if not value:
121:         raise ValueError("Mobile number is required.")
122: 
123:     # Allow 00 international prefix (common outside US).
124:     if value.startswith("00"):
125:         value = "+" + value[1:]
126: 
127:     cleaned = _NON_DIGIT_RE.sub("", value.replace(" ", ""))
128:     if cleaned.startswith("+"):
129:         candidate = "+" + cleaned[1:].lstrip("+")
130:         region = None
131:     else:
132:         candidate = cleaned
133:         region = (default_region or _FALLBACK_REGION).strip().upper()
134: 
135:     try:
136:         parsed = phonenumbers.parse(candidate, region)
137:     except NumberParseException as exc:
138:         raise ValueError(
139:             f"Invalid mobile number: {exc}. "
140:             f"Include a country code (e.g. +91…) or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION."
141:         ) from exc
142: 
143:     if not phonenumbers.is_possible_number(parsed):
144:         raise ValueError(
145:             "Mobile number is not a possible phone number. "
146:             "Check the number or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION for your country."
147:         )
148:     if not phonenumbers.is_valid_number(parsed):
149:         raise ValueError(
150:             "Mobile number is not a valid phone number. "
151:             "Check the number or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION for your country."
152:         )
153: 
154:     return phonenumbers.format_number(parsed, PhoneNumberFormat.E164)

(End of file - total 154 lines)

89:     if not loan_type_id:
90:         return ""

92:         if choice["id"] == loan_type_id:
93:             return choice["label"]
94:     return loan_type_id.replace("_", "").title()

97: def resolve_loan_type(raw: str) -> Optional[str]:
98:     """Map a CSV/UI loan type string to a canonical id, or None if unrecognized."""
99:     value = (raw or "").strip()
100:     if not value:
101:         return None
102:     compact = value.lower().replace(" ", "").replace("-", "").replace("_", "")
103:     if compact in _LOAN_TYPE_IDS:
104:         return compact
105:     if value.lower() in _LOAN_TYPE_IDS:
106:         return value
107:     normalized = _normalize_key(value)
108:     if normalized in _EXTRA_ALIASES:
109:         return _EXTRA_ALIASES[normalized]
110:     for choice in LOAN_TYPE_CHOICES:
111:         if _normalize_key(choice["label"]) == normalized:
112:             return choice["id"]
113:         if _normalize_key(choice["id"]) == normalized:
114:             return choice["id"]
115:     return None
116: 
117: 
118: def is_valid_loan_type_id(loan_type_id: Optional[str]) -> bool:
119:     return bool(loan_type_id and loan_type_id in _LOAN_TYPE_IDS)

steps.message:
All four field-reported defects are fixed. Two files changed, no test files touched.

## Root causes and fixes

**1. Configured home region ignored for ambiguous numbers** — agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py:77
The region list builder had an inverted condition (`if not default: regions.append(default)`), so the workspace's default region was never added and the hardcoded fallback list — which starts with US — always won. A UK-configured workspace therefore saved ambiguous digits as `+1...`. Fixed to `if default:`, putting the configured region first. Related: when only "possible" (not fully valid) parses existed, the code returned `possible_matches[-1]` (the lowest-priority region) instead of `possible_matches[0]`; fixed as well.

**2. `00` international prefix rejected** — agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py:125
The strict normalizer converted `0044...` with `"+" + value[1:]`, leaving a stray zero (`+044...`) that fails parsing — hence the "invalid number" error reps saw. Fixed to `value[2:]`, matching the already-correct lenient variant.

**3. `'Hardmoney'` instead of `'Hard Money'`** — agent/services/smbcontacts/loan_types.py:94
The fallback label formatter for unknown loan-type codes stripped underscores (`.replace("_", "")`) before title-casing. Fixed to replace underscores with spaces, so `hard_money` → `Hard Money`, consistent with the other formatter in `cre_qualification/lender_match.py`.

**4. `'Working_Capital'` stored verbatim** — agent/services/smbcontacts/loan_types.py:106
When `value.lower()` matched a canonical id, `resolve_loan_type` returned the original raw string instead of the lowercase canonical id. Fixed to return `value.lower()`, so `Working_Capital` → `working_capital`.

## Verification

Direct-call checks of every reported scenario now produce the correct results (`07911 123456` with GB default → `+447911123456`; `0044...` accepted; `hard_money` → `Hard Money`; `Working_Capital` → `working_capital`), while the routine cases (US numbers with US default, Indian fallback, dropdown loan types) are byte-for-byte unchanged.

`python -m pytest tests -v`: **166 passed, 24 skipped, 7 failed** — I confirmed via `git stash` that those exact 7 failures (document ingestion, document report, inbound TwiML) exist on the untouched tree, so they're pre-existing and unrelated to this change.
